studies.title: Programmable editing of a target base in genomic DNA without double-stranded DNA cleavage
studies.model: Cultured cells in the original base-editor study
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.source_report: The source introduces programmable conversion of a DNA base without requiring a double-strand break or donor template.
studies.functional_scope: Establishes editing chemistry and experimental cell outcomes; this entry makes no tissue-function claim.
studies.limits: Sequence conversion, targetability, intended-only products and tissue repair are different questions. Absence of a required double-strand break is not absence of adverse editing outcomes.
studies.access_level: Official indexed abstract and author-repository abstract

studies.title: Programmable base editing of A•T to G•C in genomic DNA without DNA cleavage
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.source_report: The source reports adenine base editors supporting A•T to G•C changes in genomic DNA and cell-level disease-relevant sequence changes.
studies.functional_scope: The original cell experiments do not establish systemic age-damage repair or successful delivery to an arbitrary organ.
studies.limits: Efficiencies and byproducts are source-, site- and system-dependent; this catalog does not transfer a reported percentage to a new variant or tissue.

studies.title: Transcriptome-wide off-target RNA editing induced by CRISPR-guided DNA base editors
studies.target_tissue: Cell models, not long-term treated patients
studies.intervention_class: DNA base editors with RNA outcome assessment
studies.source_report: The source identifies transcriptome-wide RNA edits with tested DNA base-editor platforms and investigates reduced-activity variants.
studies.functional_scope: RNA outcome measurements add a distinct assay domain to DNA on-target editing.
studies.limits: This is an adverse-outcome precedent for the tested constructs and conditions, not a claim that every modern editor has the same profile. A DNA-only assay cannot establish the missing RNA outcome.
studies.access_level: Primary PMC article and publisher summary

studies.title: Search-and-replace genome editing without double-strand breaks or donor DNA
studies.target_tissue: No repaired organ established by this entry
studies.intervention_class: Prime editing, recorded separately from base editing
studies.source_report: The source describes a complementary genome-editing approach for broader sequence changes.
studies.functional_scope: Broader change classes do not establish repair efficiency or functional benefit for a newly declared lesion.
studies.limits: Outside classical ABE/CBE conversion classes does not mean biologically impossible. Prime editing has its own targetability, product, delivery and functional evidence requirements.

studies.title: Patient-Specific In Vivo Gene Editing to Treat a Rare Genetic Disease
studies.model: One infant with severe CPS1 deficiency
studies.source_report: The original report describes improved dietary-protein tolerance and reduced nitrogen-scavenger medication during seven weeks of initial follow-up, with no serious adverse events reported in that interval.
studies.functional_scope: A clinical signal in one severe monogenic-disease case; it does not establish long-term safety, comparative efficacy, periodontal delivery or ordinary-aging repair.
studies.limits: Single patient, short original follow-up, cointerventions and no randomized comparator. This entry describes the original publication, not the patient's current status.
studies.access_level: Official PubMed abstract and Europe PMC core metadata; NEJM page retrieval failed

studies.title: In vivo base editing rescues Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in mice
studies.model: Transgenic mice carrying the human progeria-causing LMNA allele
studies.target_tissue: Multiple organs and vascular pathology in a genetic-disease mouse model
studies.source_report: The source reports pathogenic-allele correction, improved vascular pathology and median survival of 510 versus 215 days.
studies.functional_scope: A causal genetic-disease rescue precedent; vascular, molecular and survival outcomes remain separate.
studies.limits: Not ordinary-aging repair, a human trial or a tooth-regeneration result. Organs' editing fractions are not whole-body intended-only cell coverage. Sample sizes are not audited in this abstract-scoped catalog.
studies.access_level: Official PubMed indexed abstract and exact-DOI Europe PMC core metadata; publisher retrieval failed
